title: Riverbend Self-Pay Observation Rate on the Hospital Account (Encounter Billing)
content:
## The rule

On a Hospital Account (Encounter Billing) account whose financial class is self-pay, which carries observation-hour charge lines (revenue code 0762), whose final bill has dropped (final bill date and service end date both recorded; as with every uninsured discount, none is owed while the stay is open or the account is still pending billing) and which is not priced under a Riverbend self-pay package (an account carrying a package price adjustment receives the package price and never this discount), Riverbend's self-pay observation rate is granted as one uninsured discount adjustment, sourced to the account's most recent observation-hour charge line by posting date (of two posted on the same day, the one recorded first), and this rule fixes its amount. The account receives that adjustment once, and an observation-hour charge line recorded after it stands receives no further observation-rate discount.

## Uninsured discounts on a self-pay account

- The uninsured discount is posted once per self-pay final-bill liability, as an uninsured discount adjustment whose source is that liability posting, at the uninsured discount percent of the liability for emergency and medically necessary services and at the elective uninsured discount percent for elective non-covered services; on a self-pay account with observation-hour charge lines whose final bill has dropped and that is not priced under a Riverbend self-pay package, and only there, one further uninsured discount sourced to the most recent observation-hour charge line carries the observation-rate discount this rule fixes.
- The uninsured discount applies to an account whose financial class is self-pay at final bill and, as the observation-rate discount priced under this rule, to the observation-hour charge lines of an account whose financial class is self-pay when the discount is posted, whose final bill has dropped and which is not priced under a Riverbend self-pay package; the non-covered-service liability postings of an insured account and the coverage-terminated postings of an account corrected to self-pay are outside this sentence.

| Account self-pay at final bill | Uninsured discount adjustments |
|---|---|
| no observation-hour charge lines | one, on the self-pay final-bill liability |
| observation-hour charge lines, final bill dropped, no package price | that one, plus one observation-rate discount on the most recent observation-hour line |
| package-priced | none; the package price adjustment instead |

## Posting the observation rate: `post_observation_rate_discount_cc1ec28d`

**Capability.** Posts Riverbend's self-pay observation-rate discount on one self-pay hospital account that carries observation-hour charges. One call books one discount adjustment of kind `UNINSURED_DISCOUNT` on the account, dated today and pointing back to the observation-hour charge line it is figured on, and lowers the account's patient balance by the amount given. The patient sees the discount on the account activity and a lower balance.

**Invocation.** Agent-side: the representative unlocks `post_observation_rate_discount_cc1ec28d` and then calls it.

**Parameters.** `customer_id` is the patient reference number of the account holder, as returned by the patient profile lookup. `encounter_id` is the hospital account (HAR) number of the account receiving the discount, as returned by the hospital-account lookup for this patient. `source_txn_id` is the reference number of the observation-hour charge line the discount points to, as shown in that account's activity list. `amount` is the discount in USD, a positive amount with 2 decimal places, stored rounded half-up to the cent exactly as given. The first three are identifiers.

**Return.** A confirmation string: adjustment reference (the new activity reference number), account, source (the charge line named), amount (USD, 2 decimal places), posted (today's date, YYYY-MM-DD) and new balance (USD, 2 decimal places, after this discount). A returned adjustment reference means the discount is on the account.
